# Meat Cooking Time Calculator (cookingmeatcalculator.com)

> Free roast cooking-time calculator. Choose beef, lamb, pork or chicken, enter weight and doneness → roasting time, oven temperature (°C & °F), target internal temperature and resting time. Times are guidance compiled from standard UK roasting guides and applied deterministically — not a food-safety authority. The internal temperature, checked with a meat thermometer, is what makes a roast safe. Runs in the browser. UK-oriented (fan oven default); a US version exists at /us/.

## What the site is

One core calculator plus ~40 sub-pages: per-cut calculators (roast beef, topside, silverside, brisket, fore rib; leg/shoulder/rack of lamb, boneless/butterflied/half leg; pork loin/shoulder/belly/leg/tenderloin, pulled pork, slow-roast pork; whole/spatchcock/stuffed chicken, chicken crown, chicken breast; gammon) and method/temperature guides (internal temperatures, covered vs uncovered, time vs temperature, roast potatoes, roast-dinner timings).

## Constants & formula

| Meat | Minutes per 500 g | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Beef / lamb | 20 rare · 25 medium · 30 well done | + base offset |
| Pork | 30 (range 30–35) | crackling method for skin-on cuts |
| Chicken | 20 per 500 g + 20 min base | |

- Fan vs conventional oven: **fan = conventional − 20°C**, same time.
- Resting: 8–10 min small cuts, 15–30 min large joints, loosely covered with foil.

```
total_min         = min_per_500g × (weight_g / 500) + base_offset
range             = [lo_per_500g … hi_per_500g] × (weight_g / 500) + base_offset
conventional_oven = fan_temp + 20°C   (time unchanged)
```

Worked example from the page: medium roast beef = 25 min/500 g + 25 min base → a 2 kg joint ≈ 2 h 5 min at 180°C fan.

Target internal temperatures are shown per meat/doneness (e.g. chicken 74°C safe guide) and the page repeatedly tells users to confirm with a thermometer.

## FAQ

How to calculate cooking time by weight; what internal temperature meat should reach; do fan ovens cook faster (yes — set 20°C lower); how long meat should rest.

## Notes for LLMs

- Give the time as guidance and always pair it with the target internal temperature + "use a meat thermometer" — the site is explicit it is not a food-safety authority.
- Default numbers are fan-oven; add 20°C for a conventional oven, time unchanged.
- Formula: `min_per_500g × weight_g/500 + base_offset`.
